This section examines Chapter 4 — From a
permutation to

a neural network (5–6 minutes) from first
principles. Keep two

questions separate: does changing the
order change the measured outcome,

and does the proposed search method beat a
matched alternative

at the same distinct-evaluation budget?
Explain the five historical branch

types: Linear; Deep MLP; Linear + Tanh;
Linear + Sigmoid;

filling five compatible slots. Show
internal dimensions remaining compatible

so every permutation creates a valid
network. Trace a single

input vector through each block. Then
distinguish three designs: early

benchmark, where only three of five
positions were truly functional;

failed deeper plain-stack redesign, where
every ordering collapsed to

chance; v4 residual bottleneck design,
where all positions mattered and

deterministic ground truth could be
enumerated. This chapter must prevent

the viewer from assuming the earliest
benchmark was already the

final benchmark design. The distinction is
part of the result.

A large ordering effect does not
automatically imply an evolutionary-search
